findings.where: Article page specimen, the pull quote ('Whichever PPP Law I am currently working on…') in its tabula ansata frame with solid dark triangles on each side, at both widths
findings.fault: The quote is static, but its frame has an edge and the same dovetail handles as the 'Write to Mark' button, so the page's one action shape also means 'quotation'. On top of that, a boxed quote with a solid triangle on each side reads as a testimonial slider with previous and next arrows. A reader taps the triangles and nothing happens.
findings.who_objects: A reader on an article page, who tries the 'arrows' to see more quotes and gets nothing. Mark too, whose one action stops looking unique once every pull quote in Angélique's posts wears the same handles.

findings.where: Hero, 'Write to Mark' button (mailto), and the site as a whole
findings.fault: The page's only way to get in touch is a mailto link, and Mark's email address is never shown as text. When no mail program is set up, which is common on a locked work laptop or in webmail-only setups, the button does nothing visible, and the visitor has no address to copy.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank staff member on a managed work machine who clicks the button and nothing opens. They cannot contact Mark, which is the page's one job.

findings.where: Palette and every heading: minium red fills the action button and also colours the hero name line, the article headline, 'CINZEL', 'LAID · WEIGHTY · SETTLED' and the texture's 'M'
findings.fault: The direction's own rule is one accent that flows to the action, but the action colour is spread across every display heading in the same Cinzel tracked capitals as the button label. Red no longer marks what can be pressed. On an article page, the reddest and heaviest thing in view is a headline you cannot act on.
findings.who_objects: A visitor scanning for how to reach Mark, who sees red capitals everywhere and gets no colour cue for where the action is. The check is the house rule that the primary action's colour is reserved.

findings.where: Motion sketch panel, the 'Lay again' button, at both widths
findings.fault: It is a button that replays the animation, but it is drawn as an underlined link, using the underline the page saves for links such as the PDF lecture link above it. It also sits about two screens below the hero aqueduct it seems to rebuild, and the panel holds only the easing curve. So if it replays the hero, pressing it shows no visible result unless the visitor scrolls back up. The parts map cannot confirm which element it replays.
findings.who_objects: Mark, or anyone reviewing the motion, who presses 'Lay again' expecting to watch the stones settle and sees nothing change in view.

findings.where: Texture tile, the 'STAND-IN' label in its outlined box
findings.fault: It is a static label, but it is set in the nav and button's tracked Cinzel capitals inside a ruled box. It looks like a small outlined secondary button sitting on the stone.
findings.who_objects: Mark, reviewing the tile, who may take it for a control. Few would notice.
